section_title: Appeals, Reviews and Questions of Law

nodes.label: Appeals, Reviews and Questions of Law
nodes.summary: Appeals against conviction/sentence, SJ reference, retrial, CFA jurisdiction, procedural compliance.

nodes.label: Appeal Against Conviction (CFI/DC)
nodes.summary: Grounds: conviction unsafe or unsatisfactory (Cap 221 s.83). Proviso: court may dismiss appeal if no substantial miscarriage of justice (s.83(1) proviso). Alternative verdict substitution: court may substitute conviction for lesser offence if jury could have convicted of it.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.83
nodes.summary: Appeal against conviction: unsafe or unsatisfactory ground; proviso if no substantial miscarriage of justice.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Ma Ka Kin (2015)
nodes.summary: Unsafe and unsatisfactory ground for appeal against conviction.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Chan Kam Ching (2008)
nodes.summary: Court may substitute conviction for lesser offence on appeal.

nodes.label: Appeal Against Sentence
nodes.summary: Grounds: sentence manifestly excessive, wrong in principle, or otherwise unlawful. Review of sentence by Secretary for Justice: under Cap 221 s.81A, SJ may refer sentence believed to be unduly lenient; Court of Appeal may increase.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.81A
nodes.summary: Secretary for Justice may refer unduly lenient sentence to Court of Appeal.

nodes.label: Reservation of Question of Law / Reference by SJ
nodes.summary: Cap 221 s.81A (reference by SJ) and s.81D (reservation by judge).

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.81D
nodes.summary: Reservation of question of law by judge to Court of Appeal.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Fu Chiu Wa (2013)
nodes.summary: Chief Executive reference to Court of Appeal under s.81D.

nodes.label: Appeal Against Discharge
nodes.summary: Prosecution may appeal against discharge of defendant before trial (Cap 221 s.81G).

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.81G
nodes.summary: Prosecution appeal against discharge of defendant before trial.

nodes.label: Retrial
nodes.summary: Court of Appeal may order retrial if conviction quashed and interests of justice require.

nodes.label: Appeal in Insanity / Unfitness Cases
nodes.summary: Special appeal routes under Cap 221 Part IV.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) Part IV
nodes.summary: Special appeal routes for insanity/unfitness cases.

nodes.label: CFA: Final Decision / Interlocutory Decision
nodes.summary: CFA only hears 'final decisions' in criminal matters; exceptions for certified questions and miscarriage.

nodes.label: Procedural Compliance and PD 4.2
nodes.summary: Perfected grounds of appeal: PD 4.2 requires precise grounds; failure may result in loss of time.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Khaw Kin Sun (2019)
nodes.summary: Compliance with PD 4.2 perfected grounds of appeal.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Malik Mohammad Tariq
nodes.summary: Loss of time for failure to prosecute appeal.

nodes.label: Appeal Conviction Flow: Conviction Entered
nodes.summary: Step 1: Conviction entered in CFI or DC.

nodes.label: Appeal Flow: Notice and Grounds
nodes.summary: Step 2: File notice of appeal and draft grounds within time limit.

nodes.label: Appeal Flow: Leave if Required
nodes.summary: Step 3: Obtain leave to appeal if required (e.g. appeals from DC).

nodes.label: Appeal Flow: Perfected Grounds
nodes.summary: Step 4: File perfected grounds of appeal per PD 4.2.

nodes.label: Appeal Flow: Unsafe/Unsatisfactory Test
nodes.summary: Step 5: Court applies unsafe/unsatisfactory test to conviction.

nodes.label: Appeal Flow: Proviso / Retrial / Substitution
nodes.summary: Step 6: Court applies proviso, orders retrial, or substitutes alternative verdict.

nodes.label: Appeal Flow: Costs and Loss of Time
nodes.summary: Step 7: Court awards costs or orders loss of time for frivolous appeals.
